The expected makespan of a random order has no closed form: the score uses the mean over a fixed, deterministic sample of 10,000 orders (splitmix64 keys, no library generator). It is an estimate, standard error about 1 to 1.6 time units.

Taillard reused initial seeds across size classes (14 pairs among the 90). Groups are size classes, so such pairs can fall on both sides of the split; in the split (16, 24) two pairs do (ta072/ta043, ta058/ta086), with different numbers of jobs, i.e. the same number stream laid out differently, not identical jobs. No training/fresh pair has identical times.
The reference (upper bound) is a best known value, not always optimal; the source publishes no order reaching it. Stated in the module text and the anchor.
Threshold 0.90 is an operating point fixed before anything was scored, not an external fact; it could not be compared with any textbook heuristic because no reference is in hand.
Detail group [1] sums finishing times over the instance's real machines only; the padded zero machines are not counted (stated in the module text).

answer_form: AssignProblem, ordered: variable k = place k in the order (assigned in index order), option = job, capacity 1 per job; n_vars = n_opts = J. Every permutation is a valid schedule and every published answer is a permutation, so no hard group. Groups: [0] makespan of the jobs placed so far (soft; equals the published objective for a complete answer), [1] sum of the finishing times of the placed jobs on the instance's machines (detail). Exposed: opt_attr (J, 20), column m = time of the job on machine m+1, zero columns after the real machines (exact: a zero-time machine appended after the last changes no makespan). Jobs are relabelled by the seed; machines are not (their order is the route).
instances_left_out: 30: ta091..ta120, the classes 200x10, 200x20 and 500x20 (files tai200_10, tai200_20, tai500_20, not fetched), by the size rule n_vars*n_opts = J*J <= 30,000 fixed before anything was scored
reference: Intended: the upper bound in the header line of each instance in Taillard's files - a best known makespan, attainable by an order, not always a proven optimum. NOT OBTAINED: the host was unreachable, and no value was typed from memory.
score_scale: Share of the way from the mean makespan of a uniformly random order (mean over a fixed sample of 10,000 orders) to the reference, cut to [0, 1]; 0 for an invalid answer. Chosen because a random order is above 0.5 on the plain ratio on every instance (already the machine lower bound is 0.66 to 0.89 of the random mean).
threshold_and_anchor: threshold = 0.90; anchor: "an operating point, not an external fact: on average nine tenths of the way from the makespan of a random order of the jobs to the upper bound in Taillard's file, a best known makespan that is not always optimal". Fixed before anything was scored; not calibrated against any method.
